title: Week 27
subtitle: The third trimester starts now. Visits get closer together from here.

baby.size: About the size of a head of cauliflower
baby.development: The brain is growing fast and the grooves are deepening. The baby has regular sleep and wake cycles. The lungs would still need help if born now, but the odds improve every week.

you.body: Your uterus is about three inches above your belly button. You may have more swelling, more heartburn, and more trouble sleeping. Shortness of breath is common as the uterus presses up.
you.mind: The third trimester is when the birth stops being abstract. If that brings anxiety rather than excitement, that is worth saying out loud to someone.

coreActions.title: Know how often visits happen now
coreActions.why: Visits go to every two weeks until 36, then weekly. Knowing the rhythm means you can plan work and childcare around it.
coreActions.detail: At each visit they check blood pressure, weight, and the baby's heartbeat, and they may measure your belly. From 36 weeks they may check your cervix. Ask what they are looking for so the numbers mean something to you.

options.label: Put the dates in your calendar
options.detail: Every two weeks from now. Book them at the front desk before you leave.

options.label: Ask what each visit checks
options.detail: It makes the appointments feel less like waiting.

coreActions.skipIf: You already know your practice's schedule.

coreActions.title: Know about the group B strep test
coreActions.why: It happens at 36 to 37 weeks and it is a swab, not a blood test. Knowing what it is for stops it being a surprise.
coreActions.detail: Group B strep is a common bacterium that many people carry without any symptoms. If you carry it, you get antibiotics in labor, which prevents passing it to the baby. It is not a sexually transmitted infection and it is not a sign of anything you did.

options.label: Read the CDC page
options.detail: Short and plain. Explains why the swab matters.

options.label: Ask at your next visit
options.detail: Ask when they do it and what happens if it is positive.

coreActions.skipIf: You have already had the swab.

coreActions.title: Finish the hospital bag
coreActions.why: You could need it any week now. A bag that is done is one less thing to think about.
coreActions.detail: ID, insurance card, phone charger with a long cable, comfortable clothes, toiletries, snacks, a going-home outfit for you and one for the baby, and the car seat in the car. Pack a bag for your support person too. Leave it by the door.

options.label: Use the hospital's list
options.detail: Shorter than the internet's version, and it is what they expect.

options.label: Pack your own ten items
options.detail: Enough. The hospital provides most of the rest.

coreActions.skipIf: Your bag is already packed and by the door.

alsoKnow.title: Shortness of breath is mechanical
alsoKnow.body: The uterus presses on the diaphragm. It eases around 36 weeks when the baby drops. If you are breathless at rest or have chest pain, call instead.

alsoKnow.title: Sleeping gets harder, and that is not practice for the baby
alsoKnow.body: It is the bump, the bladder, and the hormones. A pillow between the knees and a dark room help. Naps are fine.

alsoKnow.title: Decide when you stop working
alsoKnow.body: There is no rule. Some people work to 39 weeks, some stop at 36. Talk to your OB about your job — a job with long shifts or heavy lifting changes the answer.

redFlags.text: A clear change in your baby's usual movement
A severe headache that will not go, or blurred vision or spots

appointments.label: Prenatal visit
appointments.note: Visits are every two weeks from now.

appointments.label: Group B strep swab
appointments.note: A quick swab. Results in a few days.
